**🚨 Behavior observed on iOS Sandbox using `in_app_purchase_storekit 0.4.3`**

When initiating a _brand-new_ purchase in Sandbox:
- `purchaseDetails.status == PurchaseStatus.restored`
- `purchaseDetails.pendingCompletePurchase == false`

This deviates from the expected behavior:
- `PurchaseStatus.purchased`
- `pendingCompletePurchase == true`

Per official [package docs](https://pub.dev/packages/in_app_purchase), purchase confirmation should generally follow this flow:
```dart
if (purchaseDetails.pendingCompletePurchase) {
  await InAppPurchase.instance.completePurchase(purchaseDetails);
}
```

so it also breaks this flow

> if I purchase a subscription using one Apple ID, then log out of the app and log in with a different user (while still using the same Apple ID), the app shows a popup stating that an active subscription already exists—even though the new user hasn’t made any purchase. It incorrectly prompts them to manually cancel the subscription and wait until it expires!

@participant9 However, the example you mentioned is actually a different case.
In your scenario, the subscription is tied to the Apple ID (which is expected, as all App Store purchases are managed at the Apple ID level), but you’re switching app users within the same device/account context.

The behavior you’re observing—preventing a duplicate purchase—is correct. Apple handles billing via Apple ID, not per app user. If you need to associate subscriptions with individual business users, you’ll need to implement your own user-access logic on top of Apple’s purchase validation, such as checking which app user has already claimed the entitlement.

So in short: subscription ownership is bound to the Apple ID, but access control within the app is your responsibility to manage.

It is problematic that the State value always becomes PurchaseStatus.restored, but the return value is also always false for pendingCompletePurchase.

If the status is PurchaseStatus.restored, even if the process is forced to run without checking pendingCompletePurchase, it will fail the App Store Connect API receipt verification.


The solution was to downgrade the in_app_purchase_storekit version.

```yaml
dependency_overrides:  
  in_app_purchase_storekit: 0.3.22
```

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
So this is definitely a bug that I introduced when I was implementing Storekit 2 into in_app_purchase_storekit. For some background on why I initially did it this way (wrongly), iirc Apple changed the way restored purchases work between Storekit 1 and 2.

In StoreKit 1, when you restored a purchase, the App Store would send back transactions that were explicitly marked as restored. This value gets pipped through, and forwarded to Dart as PurchaseStatus.restored.

However, with StoreKit 2, there is no longer a concept of a restored purchase. When you initiate a restore, like with AppStore.sync(), Storekit 2 will just refresh your transaction history, then deliver any valid past purchases through the Transaction.updates stream. However, these purchase "look" identical to brand-new purchases - theres no longer a field that conveniently marks for us when it's a restored purchase vs a fresh purchase.

I think what I was trying to do was to "guess" when a purchase was being restored by seeing if a transaction had a receipt is attached to it - however I didn't realize all valid transactions have a receipt, which means it results in every single purchase being marked as restored. 

There is some difficulty in getting this right as I only have access to a sandbox environment, but I'm theorizing a better flow would be to set a flag `isRestoring` after `restorePurchases()` is called, and mark any new transaction thats pushed through the Transaction.updates stream while `isRestoring` is true as `PurchaseStatus.restored`.

If anyone in the community has a better insight on how this *should* work please let me know - you all have much deeper knowledge than I do on what the expected behaviour should be. I'm really really sorry about any issues you guys may have run into, so please bear with me a little longer!

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
> However, with StoreKit 2, there is no longer a concept of a restored purchase. When you initiate a restore, like with AppStore.sync(), Storekit 2 will just refresh your transaction history, then deliver any valid past purchases through the Transaction.updates stream. However, these purchase "look" identical to brand-new purchases - theres no longer a field that conveniently marks for us when it's a restored purchase vs a fresh purchase.


> If anyone in the community has a better insight on how this _should_ work please let me know - you all have much deeper knowledge than I do on what the expected behaviour should be. I'm really really sorry about any issues you guys may have run into, so please bear with me a little longer!

In StoreKit 2 there’s no longer a concept of a “restored” purchase — [`AppStore.sync()`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/appstore/sync()) just re-fetches transaction history and any valid past purchases are re-emitted on `Transaction.updates` exactly like new ones. Because of that, we can’t reliably infer restoration by setting a flag before calling `sync()`: the user might cancel the system prompt, or no transactions might come through, leaving us unsure when to clear the flag. Essentially, “restoring” is not a distinct event in SK2, so there’s no safe way to tag transactions as restored without guesswork.
